Introduction\nEHR (Electronic Health Record) systems provide means for exporting PHI (Protected Health Information)\nto allow healthcare providers to share information efficiently while maintaining the privacy and security\nof patient data. Compulink Advantage offers access to the application and files that allow users of export\nfiles to access export format documentation to process EHI after it has been exported by the Advantage\nproduct.\nThis documentation guide will provide the user an understanding of the resulting files from the PHI\nExport. It will explain how to read the files, understand the meaning behind fields and connections, and\noffer other insight to properly make use of this extensive amount of information. For information on how\nto run this function or any other function or tool in Compulink Advantage please refer to the eLearning\nHelp Manual and Compulink University content made available to all users.\n\n2. Understanding the Files\nAs per requirements an export may contain one patient, or a full collection of patients. The result will be\na password protected ZIP file. The password is provided when the function completes.\nInside this collection you will find a series of files containing the patient demographics, medical records,\nbilling records, images, and more.\n\na. Tables\nThese files will be exported as a flat CSV file.\nThe naming structure will be P###_TABLENAME.csv. Where ### is the patient identifier number, and\nTABLENAME is the table data referenced.\nFor example, P20_EXAMDIAG.csv would be patient ID: 20, Exam Diagnosis table.\n\nb. Images\nThese files will be exported in their native image format. Generally, but not limited to PDF, PNG, and\nJPG.\nThe naming structure will be P###_E/D###_####.csv. Where ### is the patient identifier number,\nE/D will either be E or D, noting this is a demographics document (D), or an exam document (E). ####\nreferences the image’s unique identifier.\nFor example, P20_E20_1579.PDF would be patient ID: 20, Exam image, Image Reference ID: 1579.\nAdditional Notes:\n▪\n▪\n\nIf a full collection of patients was exported instead of a single patient, the P###_ identifier\nwill be noted a P0_.\n.FLD files are discussed in Section 3 below.\n\nONC Cures 2023 RWT Plan | ©Compulink 2023 | v 09.20.2023\n\nPage 4\n\n\f170.315(b) (10) Electronic Health Information (EHI) Export\n\n3. Linking the Files\nPerhaps the most important piece of using this collection of files is understanding how they work\ntogether to build out a complete picture for the resulting patient(s). At a high-level, every file involved\nwith a single patient will be abbreviated with the same P###_ identifier as explained in the section\nabove. For a collection of patients, the table file will include all patients in one file per table.\nTaking a step down, and focusing on the CSV file, its broken up into two categories. Demographics/Billing\nrelated files and Exam related files.\n\na. Demographics/Billing related files\nThese are all the CSV files where the table name does not start with EXAM. Their unique identifiers\nmay be referenced in an exam, but they are not exam specific. The key field is the Patient Identifier\nNumber, otherwise known as the PATUNIQUE. For key demographic information, *_PATIENT.csv\nshould be used.\n\nb. Exam related files\nThese are all the CSV files where the table name starts with EXAM. The EXAM table itself is the\nprominent table (*_EXAM.csv), and every other EXAM[SUB TABLE NAME] will link back to a specific\nexam via the Exam Identification Number, otherwise known as the EXAMUNIQUE.\n\nc. Image files\nAs exampled in the previous section there are (D) and (E) image files. For Demographics Images (D),\nthe image unique identifier can be matched up with the DOCUNIQUE found in the DOCUMENT table\nCSV file for additional information.\nFor Exam Images (E) the image unique identifier can be matched up with the IMAGUNIQUE found in\nthe EXAMIMAG table CSV file for additional information.\n\n3. Introduction\nEHR (Electronic Health Record) systems provide means for exporting PHI (Protected Health Information)\nto allow healthcare providers to share information efficiently while maintaining the privacy and security\nof patient data. Compulink Advantage offers access to the application and files that allow users of export\nfiles to access export format documentation to process EHI after it has been exported by the Advantage\nproduct.\nThis documentation guide will provide the user an understanding of the resulting files from the PHI\nExport. Understanding the Files\nAs per requirements an export may contain one patient, or a full collection of patients. The result will be\na password protected ZIP file. The password is provided when the function completes.\nInside this collection you will find a series of files containing the patient demographics, medical records,\nbilling records, images, and more.\n\na. Tables\nThese files will be exported as a flat CSV file.\nThe naming structure will be P###_TABLENAME.csv. Where ### is the patient identifier number, and\nTABLENAME is the table data referenced.\nFor example, P20_EXAMDIAG.csv would be patient ID: 20, Exam Diagnosis table.\n\nb. Images\nThese files will be exported in their native image format. Generally, but not limited to PDF, PNG, and\nJPG.\nThe naming structure will be P###_E/D###_####.csv. Where ### is the patient identifier number,\nE/D will either be E or D, noting this is a demographics document (D), or an exam document (E). ####\nreferences the image’s unique identifier.\nFor example, P20_E20_1579.PDF would be patient ID: 20, Exam image, Image Reference ID: 1579.\nAdditional Notes:\n▪\n▪\n\nIf a full collection of patients was exported instead of a single patient, the P###_ identifier\nwill be noted a P0_.\n.FLD files are discussed in Section 3 below.\n\nONC Cures 2023 RWT Plan | ©Compulink 2023 | v 09.20.2023\n\nPage 4\n\n\f170.315(b) (10) Electronic Health Information (EHI) Export\n\n3. Linking the Files\nPerhaps the most important piece of using this collection of files is understanding how they work\ntogether to build out a complete picture for the resulting patient(s). At a high-level, every file involved\nwith a single patient will be abbreviated with the same P###_ identifier as explained in the section\nabove. For a collection of patients, the table file will include all patients in one file per table.\nTaking a step down, and focusing on the CSV file, its broken up into two categories. Demographics/Billing\nrelated files and Exam related files.\n\na. Demographics/Billing related files\nThese are all the CSV files where the table name does not start with EXAM. Their unique identifiers\nmay be referenced in an exam, but they are not exam specific. The key field is the Patient Identifier\nNumber, otherwise known as the PATUNIQUE. For key demographic information, *_PATIENT.csv\nshould be used.\n\nb. Exam related files\nThese are all the CSV files where the table name starts with EXAM. The EXAM table itself is the\nprominent table (*_EXAM.csv), and every other EXAM[SUB TABLE NAME] will link back to a specific\nexam via the Exam Identification Number, otherwise known as the EXAMUNIQUE.\n\nc. Image files\nAs exampled in the previous section there are (D) and (E) image files. For Demographics Images (D),\nthe image unique identifier can be matched up with the DOCUNIQUE found in the DOCUMENT table\nCSV file for additional information.\nFor Exam Images (E) the image unique identifier can be matched up with the IMAGUNIQUE found in\nthe EXAMIMAG table CSV file for additional information.\n\n3.
